questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding the slow start phase of the TCP congestion control algorithm. Note that $cwnd$ stands for the TCP congestion window and MSS denotes the Maximum Segment Size.

(i) The $cwnd$ increases by 2 MSS on every successful acknowledgment.
(ii) The $cwnd$ approximately doubles on every successful acknowledgement.
(iii) The $cwnd$ increases by 1 MSS every round trip time.
(iv) The $cwnd$ approximately doubles every round trip time.

Which one of the following is correct?
explanation:
In the TCP Slow Start phase:

1. For every successful ACK received, $cwnd$ increases by $1\text{ MSS}$.
2. Because each ACK increases $cwnd$ by $1\text{ MSS}$, receiving ACKs for all segments sent in one Round Trip Time (RTT) results in doubling the $cwnd$ every RTT (exponential growth).

Evaluating the statements:
• (i) Incorrect: $cwnd$ increases by $1\text{ MSS}$ per ACK, not $2\text{ MSS}$.
• (ii) Incorrect: $cwnd$ doubles per RTT, not per individual ACK.
• (iii) Incorrect: Increasing $cwnd$ by $1\text{ MSS}$ per RTT is characteristic of the Congestion Avoidance phase, not Slow Start.
• (iv) Correct: $cwnd$ approximately doubles every round trip time during the Slow Start phase.

Hence, only (iv) is true.
